# Alloy Robotics Raises $8 Million At $80 Million Valuation To Help Engineers Debug Robot Fleets With AI Agents By Amit Chowdhry Today at 10:26 AM Alloy Robotics has raised $8 million at an $80 million valuation to scale an AI platform that helps engineers diagnose failures across robot fleets by automatically analyzing massive amounts of operational data\. Square Peg led the round, with existing investors Blackbird, Airtree, and Skip Capital returning\. The financing also included leaders and engineers from OpenAI, Anthropic, Tesla, Waymo, Halter, and Carbon Robotics, along with several Alloy customers\. The latest round brings Alloy’s total funding to approximately $10\.5 million just over a year after the company was founded\. Alloy is tackling one of the more difficult operational problems emerging as robotics companies move from individual prototypes to large fleets operating in real-world environments\. When a robot fails, engineers can spend hours, days, or even weeks examining telemetry, logs, sensor output, video, software changes, and other information to determine what went wrong\. # Skild AI tops robotics funding with $2\.2B raised, valued at over $14B Skild AI, a robotics startup that didn’t even exist three years ago, has now raised more than $2\.2 billion in total funding\. Its latest round, a $1\.4 billion Series C closed in January 2026, valued the company at over $14 billion\. That’s the largest reported robotics AI funding round to date, and it tripled the company’s valuation in just seven months\. ## From zero to $14 billion in record time Skild AI was founded in 2023 by Deepak Pathak and Abhinav Gupta\. The company emerged from stealth in July 2024 with a $300 million Series A that valued it at $1\.5 billion\. A seed round of approximately $14\.5 million preceded that, and a Series B followed, pushing the valuation to around $4\.5 billion\. Then came the Series C\. SoftBank led the $1\.4 billion round, joined by a roster of investors that reads like a who’s-who of tech capital: NVIDIA’s NVentures, Bezos Expeditions, Lightspeed, Coatue, and Sequoia Capital\. The round is in progress, and details could change\. Generalist AI and 8VC did not respond to requests for comment\. It's the latest example of investors pouring money into physical AI AI systems that can act in the real world\. Generalist is competing with startups like Physical Intelligence, valued at more than $11 billion, Skild AI, valued at more than $14 billion, Field AI, valued at $2 billion, and Genesis AI, which is in talks to raise funding at a $3 billion valuation\. The fresh funding comes just one month after Generalist announced it had raised $400 million to develop more sophisticated AI models for robots\. # Former SpaceX Engineers Open Cincinnati Factory for Aerospace Manufacturing - Newsy Today An autonomous steel fabrication factory launched in Camp Washington by three former SpaceX engineers has secured $15 million in seed funding to expand its artificial intelligence-powered manufacturing technology, according to company announcements\. The startup, named 1872, stated that the investment is among the largest seed funding rounds in Ohio history and was led through private funds advised by The O\.H\.I\.O\. Fund\. ## Inside the Camp Washington Autonomous Steel Factory Operating out of the historic David Hummel Building Company site on Spring Grove Avenue, the facility spans a 1903 industrial property originally tied to the construction of Cincinnati City Hall and Union Terminal\. According to company leadership, the factory combines artificial intelligence software with robotic welding technology supplied by Columbus-based Path Robotics to streamline the production of steel components for modular construction and infrastructure projects\. The startup aims to achieve full factory automation by 2027, reducing reliance on manual labor for routine fabrication tasks\. **Did you know?**
